sources.title: m3_connectivity.py: matrices, tests and exhaustive check for module m3
sources.venue: Written for this paper by module m3; output saved beside it
sources.notes: Pure Python integer arithmetic. Output is in scripts/m3_connectivity.out. The exhaustive check compares the matrix tests with a breadth-first search on every labelled simple graph with N up to 6; it is a computation, not a proof, and the breadth-first search is the comparison oracle.

claims.text: In a simple graph, for distinct vertices u and v, the following are equivalent: there is a (u,v)-walk (Definition 1.2.10); there is a (u,v)-path in the textbook sense of Definition 1.2.12 (no repeated edge, English trail); there is a simple (u,v)-path (Definition 1.2.13, no repeated vertex). Hence Definition 2.1.1 of connected means the same whichever of the three is read as 'path', and it agrees with the board's definition under the course convention. Proof: a trail is a walk by definition; a walk contains a simple path (Lemma 1.2.1); a simple path of length at least 1 in a simple graph has distinct edges, so it is a trail.

support.quote: G գրաֆի (u0, uk)-ճանապարհը կանվանենք պարզ (u0, uk)-ճանապարհ, եթե նրա մեջ մտնող բոլոր գագաթները զույգ առ զույգ տարբեր են:
Ենթադրենք, որ G գրաֆում u-ն և v-ն իրարից տարբեր երկու գագաթներ են: Այդ դեպքում ցանկացած (u, v)-շրջանցումից կարելի է առանձնացնել պարզ (u, v)-ճանապարհ:
եթե e1,…,ek-ն G գրաֆի զույգ առ զույգ տարբեր կողեր են:

claims.text: If there is a walk of length k from u to v with u different from v in a simple graph, there is a simple (u,v)-path of length at most k. Proof: take a (u,v)-walk of least length; if it repeated a vertex, deleting the stretch between the two visits gives a shorter (u,v)-walk, a contradiction; so it is a simple path, and its length is at most k. This supplies the length bound that textbook Lemma 1.2.1 does not state. The case u = v is not needed for the test.

support.quote: Assume that there is a walk from u to v of length k for some k ∈ N. Then, there is a path from u to v of length ≤ k.
Ենթադրենք, որ G գրաֆում u-ն և v-ն իրարից տարբեր երկու գագաթներ են: Այդ դեպքում ցանկացած (u, v)-շրջանցումից կարելի է առանձնացնել պարզ (u, v)-ճանապարհ:

claims.text: Connectivity test, proved: a simple graph with N >= 2 vertices is connected if and only if every off-diagonal entry of S = A + A^2 + ... + A^(N-1) is positive. The proof uses the walk-counting theorem (C5, m1, which also gives that all entries are non-negative integers), Lemma 3.2 (M3-2) and the bound that a simple path has length at most N - 1 (C18). For N = 1 the graph is connected and there is nothing to test. Paramadevan and Sotheeswaran state the same test; their proof is incomplete (C23). This claim gives the full proof for C24, which stays at the base file's confidence.

support.quote: Then, AG is connected if and only if bij 6= 0, when i 6= j.
However, any path from u to v must have length ≤ n − 1, where n is the number of vertices of G (since a path of length k has k + 1 distinct vertices, but G has only n vertices to spare).

claims.text: Equivalent form: for N >= 1, G is connected if and only if (I + A)^(N-1) has no zero entry. Proof: I commutes with A, so the binomial theorem gives (I + A)^(N-1) as the sum over k = 0..N-1 of C(N-1,k) A^k with every binomial coefficient at least 1; all terms are non-negative, so an off-diagonal entry is positive exactly when S has a positive entry there, and every diagonal entry is at least 1 from the k = 0 term. No source read states this in this form (see C24).

support.locator: scripts/m3_connectivity.out, item 6, binomial check on the board graph
support.quote: (I+A)^2 equals sum C(2,k) A^k for k=0..2 on board graph: True

claims.text: For distinct i and j, n_i and n_j lie in the same connectivity component if and only if S_ij > 0. So the zero pattern of S off the diagonal marks which pairs are in different components (Remark 2.1.1 of the textbook: one component if and only if connected).

support.quote: Դիտողություն 2.1.1: G գրաֆը կապակցված է այն և միայն այն դեպքում, երբ այն ունի կապակցվածության մեկ բաղադրիչ:
Then, u ≃G v if and only if there exists a path from u to v.

claims.text: For distinct i and j in the same component, the textbook distance d(n_i, n_j) (Definition 1.2.16) equals the least k >= 1 with (A^k)_{ij} > 0. Proof: a walk of that length exists; if a shorter path existed it would give a smaller k; and a shortest walk is a path (Lemma 3.2).

support.quote: կսահմանենք որպես կարճագույն (u, v)-ճանապարհի երկարություն, եթե G գրաֆում գոյություն ունի առնվազն մեկ (u, v)-ճանապարհ, և +∞՝ հակառակ դեպքում:

claims.text: Neither the upper limit N - 1 nor the sum can be dropped. On the three-vertex path graph of the board, (A^2)_{12} = 0 although the graph is connected, so a single power does not suffice. On path graphs with N = 3, 4, 5, 6 vertices, the first power with a positive (1,N) entry is exactly N - 1, so a limit below N - 1 would miss pairs.

support.quote: path graph on N=6: least k with (A^k)_(1,N) > 0 is 5 = N-1: True
A^2 alone on the board graph (connected), entry (1,2): 0

claims.text: Worked examples, computed by script. Board graph (edges n_1n_2, n_2n_3): A^2 has rows 1 0 1 / 0 2 0 / 1 0 1; S has rows 1 1 1 / 1 2 1 / 1 1 1; (I+A)^2 has rows 2 2 1 / 2 3 2 / 1 2 2; connected. Disconnected graph (edge n_1n_2 only, n_3 isolated): A^2 has rows 1 0 0 / 0 1 0 / 0 0 0; S has rows 1 1 0 / 1 1 0 / 0 0 0; (I+A)^2 has rows 2 2 0 / 2 2 0 / 0 0 1; zero entries at (1,3) and (2,3) and their mirrors. Triangle (the board drawing read as three edges): every entry of S is 2 and every entry of (I+A)^2 is 3; connected.

On every labelled simple graph with N = 1 to 6 vertices (1, 2, 8, 64, 1024 and 32768 graphs) the S-test and the (I+A)^(N-1) test agree with a breadth-first search from n_1; the counts of connected graphs are 1, 1, 4, 38, 728 and 26704.

support.quote: N=6: labelled graphs 32768, connected 26704, test disagrees with BFS: 0

claims.text: Breadth-first search as the alternative: starting at n_1, repeatedly visit the unvisited neighbours (columns with entry 1 in the current row of A); G is connected if and only if all N vertices are visited. The BFS tree property (tree path from the root is a shortest path) is in Grinberg; the connectivity use follows from it and from M3-5 and is the module's own reading, not stated as such by the source. The remark that the matrix test needs N - 2 matrix products while BFS reads each row of A at most once is the module's own count and is not sourced.

support.locator: Section on spanning trees, printed p. 176
support.quote: the path from r to v in this spanning tree is a shortest path from r to v in G. For this reason, this spanning tree is called a breadth-first search (“BFS”) tree.
